reviewedAssessments.topic: Accepted clocks versus new candidate clocks
reviewedAssessments.assessment: Accepted1800second idle and28800second original absolute boundaries remain conjunctive with current authority and token validity. Only first guarded unique allowlisted business admission refreshes idle once; pending effect is separate, replay/read/status/socket setup/renewal/output cannot.900second mandatory renewal and60second prior recovery are explicitly new unmeasured candidates requiring integrated adoption, not standards or founder-approved values.

PostgreSQL security metadata/epoch family is a recommendation under existing architecture, not an adopted table/migration/retention mapping. Principal enabled/security epoch, session state/epoch and current action/object/purpose guards are separate from JWT claims; Redis cannot reconstruct authority or bypass lost required limits. Principal then session then independent object guard ordering, trusted time after all waits, no rollback grace and overflow failure are coherent requirements. Concrete locking, row/column mapping, failover clock precision and deadlock/rollback behavior remain physical proof.

reviewedAssessments.topic: Due current token versus expired/retired token
reviewedAssessments.assessment: Mandatory renewal_due additionally removes business admission/private business output even if JWT exp is later. A due but still-valid current credential has only bounded control/status/CSRF/renewal/logout eligibility; it is not a business refresh grant. Signature/type/issuer/audience/key/claims/current-record checks plus session clock still apply. An expired token cannot be accepted merely because idle/absolute session state remains eligible. The exact fixed token-expiry policy is not yet selected; do not infer expiry equals900seconds or original absolute from this logical candidate.

reviewedAssessments.topic: One successor, one bounded immediate-prior recovery
reviewedAssessments.assessment: Guarded due rotation creates one successor and moves only old current into at most one recovery slot, capped by cutover+60, old token expiry and current session boundary. Early current calls re-deliver the same current claims/identity/times/key association. Prior is recovery-only with current session CSRF/source guards; it cannot send/read business, mint tickets, renew idle or fork another successor. Concurrent old requests converge on the same current generation. Authentic stale reuse after its window denies rather than automatically revoking a legitimate other session.

Reconstruction retains exact existing minimal claims/identity/original times and signing association, without ordinary raw-JWT storage; missing safe key/source material fails closed. Final credential response rechecks current authority. Late Set-Cookie can overwrite browser bytes, but cannot revive revoked/retired/replaced server authority; current/prior recovery or fresh sign-in may be needed. Client epochs/tab hints do not guarantee network cookie order or serve as server authority.

Normal omission of both Max-Age/Expires is compatible with the existing conditional any-persistent-expiry cap. It avoids a stale browser-side idle deadline after later qualifying socket commands. Server token/session/generation validity still controls; browser close/restore is not logout. Exact Secure/HttpOnly/Lax/Path, host-only existing cookie identity, no JWT in JS/body/storage/Bearer fallback, current session-bound independent CSRF and exact logout deletion remain. Same eligible login may retain CSRF across short JWT rotation; fresh login/replacement/revocation cannot reuse its proof.

reviewedAssessments.topic: Channel cutover, immutable effects and operation truth
reviewedAssessments.assessment: Token rotation fences old token-bound channel/ticket/queued output and requires current reinitialization/reconciliation before readiness. It does not end/reassign conversations, change availability, cancel booking or automatically replay text. Already-admitted business intent retains immutable meaning and uncertain effects; later actor/service/object/purpose guards remain mandatory, not a saved JWT. No session-loss inference about effect cancellation or duplicate-operation permission.

reviewedAssessments.topic: Output admission and final writer linkage
reviewedAssessments.assessment: One already-serialized bounded projection/frame rechecks every principal/session/token/object/purpose/source/copy generation immediately before final writer handoff, including operator returned/lookahead/anchor dependencies. The guarded nonblocking writer handoff must serialize with rotation/revocation/expiry across workers; an old verdict cannot be reused by a delayed local queue. The candidate expressly rejects DB commit or cache notification as proof and forbids unbounded network/provider I/O inside a DB transaction. Physical proof is a genuine adoption prerequisite; already admitted bytes may arrive later and cannot be recalled.

reviewedAssessments.topic: Revocation, privilege changes and Entra signal limits
reviewedAssessments.assessment: Logout invalidates exact current session/CSRF/token/channel/output generations with source/proof guards; repeated invalid-session logout cannot revoke a different eligible session. Principal-wide security epoch provides current admission fencing rather than socket enumeration/JWT expiry. Privilege change cannot silently elevate an existing session. Microsoft logout is distinct; optional signal requires verified exact binding, and unknown required Entra freshness denies. Restore cannot resurrect old epochs or infer cleanup from process death.

Security records retain existing identifying/secret protection with exact policy still held. Recovery/new sign-in preserves only currently permitted source/work/draft state after fresh principal/object/assignment/consent checks; no longer transcript, expired proof, browser transcript cache or historic-copy grant. Warning/focus/TL-WARN-EXTEND and complete-process accessibility remain required; transport renewal cannot be fake More time or user activity.

independentLogicalCases.case: Two tabs use A at due time; both renew concurrently.
independentLogicalCases.result: Session guard permits A->B once. Immediate prior A can re-deliver only B within its original recovery bound; early valid B cannot allocateC or extend clocks.

independentLogicalCases.case: B cookie response is lost while A and current CSRF remain available.
independentLogicalCases.result: Protected immediate-prior recovery may re-deliver existing B, with original B times/key association and no extended A recovery. Unknown key/source/session state fails closed.

independentLogicalCases.case: A is prior but a reloaded/new tab has no current in-memory CSRF proof.
independentLogicalCases.result: This candidate gives prior A only CSRF-protected recovery, not CSRF retrieval or private business. It cannot bootstrap proof from prior bearer alone; fresh deliberate sign-in may be necessary. No promise that every lost-cookie/reload case recovers within60seconds.

independentLogicalCases.case: JWT expiry is reached while authoritative idle/absolute session state is still eligible.
independentLogicalCases.result: Do not accept expired JWT or invent a browser refresh secret. The remaining fixed-expiry binding must define the intended available renewal interval; until a valid credential/control path exists, use safe failure/reauthentication.900second due is a separate eligibility clock, not an assumed exp value.

independentLogicalCases.case: Browser sleeps beyond due but resumes before all current token/session boundaries.
independentLogicalCases.result: Still-valid current credential may enter bounded deliberate renewal without business activity; expired credential, idle/absolute expiry or unknown freshness cannot be repaired by changing clocks.

independentLogicalCases.case: Early A credential response is handed off while valid, then A->B happens and the old response arrives last.
independentLogicalCases.result: Browser may retain A. Server currentness remains B; only applicable recovery or fresh sign-in can restore use. No exactly-once cookie ordering or old-server authority revival is claimed.

independentLogicalCases.case: Authentic A arrives after immediate-prior recovery ends.
independentLogicalCases.result: Deny without restoring A, extending the grace window or automatically killing another legitimate current session. Authorized security-risk response remains separate.

independentLogicalCases.case: Rotation approaches original absolute expiry, or idle expires while a request waits on guards.
independentLogicalCases.result: Trusted time after guards plus strict earliest boundary denies at equality; renewal/control cannot reset original absolute or expired idle activity. Prior lifetime cannot outlive earlier token/session bounds.

independentLogicalCases.case: Text/business operation is admitted before cutover; private output or external work remains unsettled.
independentLogicalCases.result: Preserve immutable operation identity and uncertainty, fence obsolete queued/token-bound output, recheck later actor/service/purpose authority and reconcile before any new command. Rotation/logout is not proof of no effect, automatic cancellation or replay permission.

independentLogicalCases.case: Logout/principal disable wins before final output handoff.
independentLogicalCases.result: All later protected admissions must see current fenced generations; old local verdict/cache/connection list is insufficient. Exact cross-worker guard-to-writer arbitration still needs physical proof.

independentLogicalCases.case: First qualifying command is pending; a retry/reconciliation repeats it.
independentLogicalCases.result: Idle updates only at first guarded admission, never again from replay/reconciliation/provider completion. Failed pre-admission/transport gestures do not manufacture activity.

independentLogicalCases.case: Prior recovery record or request accounting has not settled when later transition/cleanup is considered.
independentLogicalCases.result: At-most-one prior record and fail-closed unknown/unsettled accounting cannot become an implicit unbounded history, overwritten necessary evidence or early release. Exact finite control capacity/drain/disposal is a required later binding.
